Broken Side and Rear Glass: Cleanup, Interior Repair and Coordination

The glass shop replaces the window. The glass that exploded into your seats, carpet, vents and door is still your problem, and so is whatever else the break damaged. That part is ours.

What we do when a window is broken

  • Complete glass removal: tempered side and rear glass breaks into thousands of pieces that end up under seats, inside door panels, in vents and defroster ducts. We remove trim and seats as needed and clear every cavity.
  • Interior repair: cut or scuffed seats, scratched panels, a dumped console, footprints and spills from the break-in.
  • Paint around the opening: scratches and scuffs on the door frame or quarter panel from the break or the tool used.
  • Weather protection: we can secure the opening with a temporary cover while the replacement glass is on the way.
  • Coordination: we schedule around the glass installer so the interior is clean before the new glass goes in, and you are not vacuuming glass out of your defroster next summer.

What we are honest about

We are a detail and restoration shop, not a glass shop. We do not stock or install glass. In Bryan–College Station there are several established auto-glass installers, and many insurers have a preferred glass network; use whichever you and your insurer prefer, and we will handle everything around it.

Windshields: windshield chips and cracks are a glass-shop job and often a separate glass-coverage claim. We do not repair windshields.

What to do right now

  1. If it was a break-in, file a police report and photograph the vehicle before touching anything.
  2. Cover the opening with plastic and tape so rain and more debris stay out.
  3. Call your insurer or glass network to arrange the replacement glass, and send us photos so the cleanup and interior repair can be scheduled around it.

Glass, cleanup and your insurance

Broken glass from a break-in or vandalism is typically part of a comprehensive claim, and some policies carry separate glass coverage with its own deductible. The interior cleanup and repair that goes with a break-in is usually part of the same claim, and we itemize it so the adjuster can see exactly what was done and why. Coverage, and what your deductible is, are always your insurance company’s decision, never ours.

We don’t bill your insurance company for you: you receive a written, itemized estimate and photos you can submit with your claim, and we work from the estimate once you decide to proceed.

Questions people ask

Do you replace car windows?

No. Glass replacement is done by a glass shop. We remove the broken glass from the interior, repair the damage the break caused and coordinate with the installer you or your insurer choose.

Why not just vacuum the glass myself?

You can get the big pieces, but tempered glass spreads into seat tracks, door panels, vents and under the carpet, and a household vacuum will not survive it. Fragments left behind come out of the vents for months and cut hands and upholstery.

Should the cleanup happen before or after the new glass?

Before is better, so the installer is not sealing new glass over a dirty channel and nothing gets trapped behind the new trim. We schedule around the glass appointment.

Will insurance pay for the cleanup?

When the glass broke in a covered event such as a break-in, the related interior cleanup and repair is usually part of the same claim, but your insurer decides. Our itemized estimate explains each line so the adjuster can see what was needed.
